title: Debugging: trace viewer, UI mode, codegen, inspector
summary: Trace viewer replays a run step by step; UI mode is a watch-mode IDE for tests; codegen records actions into code; the inspector steps through a test live.
why: Reading a trace is faster than re-running a test ten times. These tools turn 'it failed in CI' into 'it failed because the button was still disabled'.
body:
Trace viewer: every run in this lab records a trace — open it from the results list. It shows actions, before/after DOM snapshots, console, network, source, and errors. Locally: npx playwright show-trace trace.zip, or drop it on trace.playwright.dev (runs fully in your browser).
UI mode: npx playwright test --ui — pick tests, watch files, time-travel through steps.
Codegen: npx playwright codegen <url> — records clicks into locator-based code (a starting point, then refactor).
Inspector: npx playwright test --debug, or await page.pause() in a test.
VS Code extension: run/debug tests from the editor, pick locators.
`npx playwright trace` (CLI) inspects traces from the terminal.
objectives: Pause a test with the inspector
pitfalls: Keeping codegen output as-is (no assertions, brittle flow).

example.code:
npx playwright test --ui                  # UI mode
npx playwright test --debug               # inspector, step through
npx playwright test --trace on            # force traces locally
npx playwright show-trace test-results/…/trace.zip
npx playwright codegen http://localhost:3000/login
